action: Started the engine-rig track's Claude Code session by pasting its launch prompt.
why_not_automatable: Nothing existed yet: no board, no dispatcher, no reflex layer, no monitor. The first session of all has to be opened by a person, and every automated launch path in this repo was built later by agents this session's descendants started.
caveat: No launch is logged anywhere. Placed a few minutes before the track's first commit (2026-07-27T10:55:18Z) and its first PARTNER_SYNC paragraph (10:55:01Z). The prompt text itself is not in the repo.

action: Started the second concurrent track session (theory-compiler) by pasting its launch prompt.
why_not_automatable: Same as H-01. CLAUDE.md's premise is two Claude Code instances that do not communicate; the only thing that could put a second one on the tree at that point was a person opening it.
caveat: This track's early commits carry the same git author as engine-rig's, so the session is visible only through its own PARTNER_SYNC paragraph (2026-07-27T11:45:00Z, reporting eight finished milestones). The launch is placed alongside engine-rig's because the milestone work is contemporaneous; the exact minute is unknown.

action: Supplied the live ARC API credential by putting ARC_API_KEY into the gitignored .env at the repo root.
why_not_automatable: Minting an ARC key needs an arcprize.org account, i.e. a human identity behind a Google/GitHub login. Later confirmation: when the browser operator finally read the account panel, the only key there (a4***a91b) was NOT the repo's key (71***05dd) under the same masking, so no agent in this fleet created the credential it has been spending all along.
caveat: .env is gitignored, so the act leaves no artifact by design. Placed just before the credential-handling commit (2026-07-27T16:02:50Z) and the first authenticated API call (16:08:52Z). It may have happened considerably earlier.

action: Confirmed the development/sealed pile cut, releasing the agents to start spending game actions on the four development-pile games.
why_not_automatable: It could have been automated, and within a day it was. PARTNER_SYNC's 16:08:52Z paragraph blocks on 'waiting for pile-cut confirmation before burning action quota' and the 16:13:10Z paragraph opens with 'the cut was confirmed by the user, so contact with the development pile began'. On 2026-07-28 the human explicitly delegated this whole class of ruling (contamination handling, claim-set scope, budget and statistical conventions) to the monitor, which is direct evidence the gate did not need a person -- it needed someone with authority, and authority was later handed over.
caveat: The confirmation is stated in the tree but not timestamped; it is bracketed by the two PARTNER_SYNC paragraphs above (16:08:52Z and 16:13:10Z).

action: Opened a third session on the baseline-arms track (bare-Claude-Code baseline arm) by pasting its launch prompt.
why_not_automatable: Predates every dispatch mechanism in the repo by 90 minutes; the monitor that would later author and dispatch tickets did not exist until 18:13Z.
caveat: Identified as a separate session because its five commits carry a distinct git author (baseline-arms@local). Placed a few minutes before its first commit at 2026-07-27T16:51:03Z.

action: Authorised installing a C++ toolchain (winlibs mingw-w64 gcc) so Fast Downward could actually be built.
why_not_automatable: It was automatable and the block was policy, not capability. The agent had already written the full recipe, verified the download URL answers HTTP 206, and installed cmake, ninja and the downward clone; the ticket's stopping rule told it to record the blocker and wait for human intervention rather than install software on its own. Once the permission arrived, the whole build took ~90 seconds and 235/235 targets, no patches.
caveat: DECISIONS.md records 'resolved after the user authorised installing it' without a time. Bracketed by the blocker write-up (2026-07-27T17:44:55Z) and the FD-connected commit (18:18:44Z).

action: Created the monitor role -- a session that only monitors and never executes, audits the tree clause by clause against Theoria.md, and writes only monitor/ -- and defined the research loop it enforces (run an experiment, let it expose a defect, locate the framework layer, fix the framework).
why_not_automatable: This is the delegation act itself: the moment the assembly job stopped being the human's. Nothing in the tree could have created a supervisory role over two sessions that could not see each other. Every later mechanism in this ledger -- board, bus, reflex, contracts, dispatch authority -- descends from this one instruction.
caveat: The role definition lives in the user's session memory, not the repo; the tree records it through the monitor's first commit (2026-07-27T18:13:55Z), monitor/spec.py's comment crediting the research loop to the user, and timeline row T-01 which classes the trigger as user_request with no incident behind it.

action: Approved the S1 full run -- haiku tier over the whole development pile, 3014 successful actions, about $103 -- clearing the budget gate the baseline-arms session had deliberately stopped at.
why_not_automatable: The money is the account owner's. BUDGET_REPORT.md is written as the gate itself ('this report is the budget gate; stop when it is written and wait for human approval'), and the track stopped there rather than sizing its own spend.
caveat: Tightly bracketed but not logged: the budget-gate commit is 2026-07-27T18:14:31Z and INC-BA-003 records harness/campaign.py landing at 18:22:16Z already self-describing as 'approved full run'. Whether the approval was a sentence from the human or the human pasting a ticket that contained it cannot be told from the tree.

action: Pasted the monitor's freshly written P-7 ticket into a session, starting a second concurrent campaign on the baseline-arms track 85 seconds after the first one began.
why_not_automatable: At this point the monitor could write tickets but had no way to launch anything; the dispatch queue, the reflex layer and the Task Scheduler path were all built the following day. A person was the transport between a written prompt and a running session -- and that is also why nothing noticed the collision: neither campaign's gate could see the other's spend.
caveat: The monitor wrote a batch of seven tickets (v3-P-1..P-7) at 18:13:55Z; only P-7's landing is provable, from INC-BA-003's process table (02:21:25 local = 18:21:25Z) and the engine-rig-authored baseline-arms commit at 18:53:26Z. How many of the other six were pasted is unknown, so this row counts one paste, not seven.

action: Instructed the monitor to externalise its whole state to a handoff file and be restarted roughly every three hours, so that a quota kill is a pause rather than amnesia.
why_not_automatable: A session cannot restart itself, and the monitor is an app session with no API behind it. The instruction is also a design call about the fleet's own supervisor, which is the one component that has no supervisor.
caveat: Attribution rests entirely on HANDOFF.md's own section heading, which credits the discipline to a user instruction of 2026-07-28. Timed at the commit that introduced that heading (2026-07-28T01:31:00Z); the instruction itself is undated.

action: Told the monitor to abolish serial ticket numbers (P-1, P-2, ...) and replace them with a two-dimensional coordinate map -- subsystem axis by stage axis -- with progress painted on the grid.
why_not_automatable: An agent could have redesigned its own numbering scheme; nothing prevented it. What the human supplied was the observation that a flat serial queue hid where the project actually was, which the monitor had been maintaining for eight hours without noticing.
caveat: Attribution rests on spec.py's own inline comment crediting the change to a user instruction. Timed just before the commit that lands it (2026-07-28T02:35:58Z).

action: Installed the claude-in-chrome extension in their own Chrome so the browser operator could drive a real, logged-in browser instead of the sandboxed in-app one.
why_not_automatable: The extension has to be installed into the human's own browser profile and that browser has to be running as them; before this, list_connected_browsers returned an empty list on four separate dispatch attempts and the ticket was abandoned three times for the same reason.
caveat: Timed to the start of the visits log's 'round 2 (after the real Chrome was connected)', bracketed above by that round's commit at 2026-07-28T03:41:00Z. The visits log deliberately records ordering, not clock times.

action: Completed the arcprize.org OAuth login in their own Chrome so the agent could read the account panel; the agent entered no credentials at any point.
why_not_automatable: Logging in is a prohibited action for the operator by contract, and it needs the account holder's identity at a Google/GitHub consent screen. The agent had correctly filed it as needs_human and refused to try alternatives.
caveat: Bracketed by the round-2 commit (2026-07-28T03:50:35Z) and the round-3 commit that reports the panel read (03:58:11Z). The panel showed an API key created at 11:48 local time (03:48Z), which is consistent.

action: Opened four Claude app sessions and pasted the ten-line boot prompts for the four standing ops agents: OPS-A drift auditor, OPS-B browser operator, OPS-M merge judge, OPS-R retrospective.
why_not_automatable: App sessions have no API. The monitor's own scaling policy states plainly that it never spawns them and can only ask the user to open one. Note what had just been made cheap, though: the long contracts had moved to monitor/ops/<ID>.md the same hour, so what the human had to paste shrank to ten lines and retuning an agent no longer costs a re-paste at all.
caveat: One row covers four pastes. loop_state.json records all four as 'booted 06:15Z' and the first TO-MONITOR check-ins are 06:15Z (OPS-B) and 06:16Z (OPS-M).

action: Opened an app session to work the V3 battery-discrimination item; it claimed the item off the board as APP-V3.
why_not_automatable: Same as H-14: no API path to an app session.
caveat: The timestamp is the session's first board claim, so the paste was somewhat earlier. Classified as human because APP-* ids have no entry in monitor/dispatch-logs/ (every machine-launched worker does).

action: Opened three more app sessions, which claimed C7-dsl-v03-mentions, A7-envelope-finish and A4a-ablation-build within the same second as APP-C7, APP-A7 and APP-P7.
why_not_automatable: Same as H-14.
caveat: One row covers three pastes; timestamp is their (identical) first board claim. Same APP-*-has-no-dispatch-log reasoning as H-15. The three claims landing in one second suggests the sessions were opened shortly before and all polled the board at once.

action: Asked for a dashboard view that answers 'what did my agents do' in plain language, rather than grids, phases and findings.
why_not_automatable: Entirely automatable -- and arguably it should have been noticed by the monitor, whose own auditor was at the same time reporting that the headline percentage had not moved across 45 commits and 14 merged branches.
caveat: Weakest row in the table. The only support is the commit's own title phrasing ('the dashboard now answers what did my agents do') plus the earlier harvester classing timeline row T-31 as user_request; the commit body credits nobody. This may have been the monitor's own initiative, in which case the row should be struck.

action: Opened two app sessions and pasted the boot prompts for the first two standing researchers: RES-1 on the online campaign and RES-2 on paper and release.
why_not_automatable: Same as H-14. App sessions also draw on a different quota pool than the headless CLI, which is exactly why this role class exists and exactly why only a person can create one.
caveat: One row covers two pastes. Timestamp is their simultaneous first board claim, about one minute after the contracts were committed (2026-07-28T10:45:26Z).

action: Granted the monitor standing authority to start, stop, scale, retask and dispatch agents without asking, reserving only two things: spending beyond the existing gate, and anything needing a human identity.
why_not_automatable: This is the second delegation act and the load-bearing one for the whole thesis: after it, headcount is a function of supply (target = min(ceiling, claimable items)) and the only hard limits are physical -- 8GB free RAM, an open quota window, territory exclusion. An agent cannot widen its own permission table; that is what a permission table is.
caveat: Timed just before the commit that records it (2026-07-28T14:14:01Z); the grant itself is undated in loop_state.json.

action: Manually poked the two standing researchers, which had each finished a round and were sitting idle waiting to be told to continue.
why_not_automatable: Fully automatable, and it was automated within the hour. The cause was a one-line contract defect: the ops contracts ended each cycle with a sleep so those agents came back by themselves, while the researcher contracts ended with 'return to step 2', a sentence with no force. The fix wrote the loop's closing explicitly, added a self-driving probe that reads a frozen heartbeat as a session waiting on a person, and sent both researchers an urgent wake-up.
caveat: The poke is not logged; it is bracketed above by the 2026-07-28T14:55:58Z bus urgent that describes it in the past tense ('you used to stop after a round and wait for the user to trigger you -- that was not your fault, it was mine'). One row covers two agents.

action: Opened two more app sessions for the newly created standing researchers RES-3 (verification) and RES-4 (infrastructure), whose contracts had been cloned from RES-1's a minute earlier.
why_not_automatable: Same as H-14. This is the clearest single measurement of what assembly delegation bought: the monitor authored two whole new roles by cloning a contract, and the human's entire share of standing up both was two pastes.
caveat: One row covers two pastes. The contracts were committed at 2026-07-28T15:06:39Z and RES-4's first board claim is 15:07:58Z (RES-3's is 15:10:01Z) -- roughly 80 seconds from 'a new role is needed' to 'it is claiming work'.

action: Approved spending on the development-pile campaign: once offline work is wrapped up, money-and-wall-clock work may start directly, with the account allowance as the only constraint.
why_not_automatable: Shared account money again. What did change is the granularity: instead of approving a run, the human approved a standing envelope, and the monitor then sized the packages itself ($200 campaign total, $60 per game, reserves of no more than $25) and issued them over the bus without asking again.
caveat: Only the upper bound is pinned: the bus order relaying the approval is timestamped 2026-07-28T15:14:17Z. loop_state.json records the grant with a date but no time, so it may have come earlier in the day.

action: Proposed writing the fleet itself up as an engineering paper plus a reusable toolkit -- the proposal that created this dataset's own work item.
why_not_automatable: An agent could have proposed it; the monitor authored its own board items all day. What it could not do is make it one of the project's directions, and the monitor's own judgement was that S17 was urgent but S18 was not -- a sequencing call it made itself once the direction was given.
caveat: Bracketed by the bus order that relays it ('the user proposed packaging this fleet as an engineering paper plus a reusable kit', 2026-07-28T15:17:38Z) and the commit that boards it (15:19:18Z).

action: Corrected the monitor's framing of the fleet study, naming the actual claim: an agent was handed assembly authority and built the fleet out of packaged agents as components, with the human's action reduced to pasting one line.
why_not_automatable: A judgement about what is novel in one's own work. The monitor had already written its version an hour earlier -- a first-hand account of how multi-agent collaboration fails -- and its own commit concedes 'the user named it better than I had'. Nothing in the fleet was checking whether the framing was the interesting one.
caveat: Bracketed by the monitor's own earlier framing (2026-07-28T15:19:18Z) and the commit recording the correction (15:22:27Z). This is the first of the two framing corrections IDEA.md records against itself.

action: Corrected the framing a second time -- rejecting the bounded concept-paper version with its applicability section as defensive -- and ruled that conception and writing wait for the main project while evidence collection continues and becomes a standing daily log.
why_not_automatable: Same class as H-24, and the monitor's own record says it drifted the same way twice within an hour (first shrinking the claim to an experience report, then to a bounded concept paper), catching neither itself. The parking half of the call is a priority ruling across the whole project, which sits above the monitor's remit.
caveat: Two decisions (the second framing correction and the park-the-idea ruling) are recorded in one commit and relayed in one bus order at 2026-07-28T15:31:43Z, so the record cannot separate them. Counted as one human turn rather than two, which is the conservative direction for a table whose shortness is the claim.

action: Reopened the RES-3 standing app session after all four standing researchers had gone silent; it immediately claimed three items.
why_not_automatable: In this harness, genuinely not: an app session whose context has filled is the one failure no API can restart, and the monitor's scaling policy says app sessions are only ever requested from the user. Note that only the action is manual -- the detection is fully automated, with the dashboard's needs_human panel naming which session died and which prompt file to paste.
caveat: Nobody logs a reopening. Placed at RES-3's first post-silence board claims (2026-07-28T19:05:22Z and 19:05:33Z), after the 18:55:16Z heartbeat that recorded all four standing sessions as dead and before the 19:45:05Z heartbeat that reports 'RES-3 restarted and immediately claimed three items'. The other three were still unreopened hours later, so this is one action, not four.
